question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

events.title: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
events.description:

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s firm grip on the Chinese Communist Party, the military, and security institutions underpins trader consensus that he will remain paramount leader past 2027. Ongoing purges of senior officials, including recent military and provincial figures, have eliminated potential rivals while installing loyalists across the Politburo and Central Military Commission. The absence of any designated successor or visible factional opposition further reduces near-term transition risks ahead of the 21st Party Congress. Analysts note that Xi, now 73, faces no evident institutional or elite pressure to step aside before completing a fourth term. Still, an abrupt health event, unexpected elite realignment, or severe economic or external shock could alter this trajectory before the congress concludes.

question: Will Gavin Newsom win the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the named individual wins and accepts the 2028 nomination of the Democratic Party for U.S. president. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Democratic Party sources.

Any replacement of the democratic nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

eventMetadata.context_description: A crowded and fluid Democratic field for the 2028 presidential nomination keeps trader probabilities closely bunched, with Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Jon Ossoff, and Gavin Newsom leading at roughly 15–21% each while Kamala Harris and others trail. No candidate has formally entered the race ahead of the 2026 midterms, leaving an open contest shaped by polling volatility, factional divides between progressives and moderates, and post-2024 positioning. Ocasio-Cortez has gained from early-state surveys and progressive momentum without committing, Ossoff’s profile has risen through Senate reelection fundraising and speeches despite repeated denials of interest, and Newsom has highlighted his record and early-state travel. Developments such as midterm outcomes, formal announcements, endorsements, or shifts in early primary states could consolidate support or elevate alternatives like Pete Buttigieg or Josh Shapiro.
